'''Luka Hudson Garza''' (born December 27, 1998) is a Bosnian-American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Boston Celtics]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) and the [[Bosnia and Herzegovina men's national basketball team|Bosnia and Herzegovina national team]].

Garza played [[college basketball]] for the [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa Hawkeyes]], where he was the consensus pick for [[List of U.S. men's college basketball national player of the year awards|national college player of the year]] for the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21 season]]. As a junior, Garza was named a consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] and [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big Ten Player of the Year]]. He played for [[Maret School]] in his hometown of [[Washington, D.C.]]

==Early life==
Garza grew up in [[Reston, Virginia]].  He learned to play basketball from his father, Frank, who played for [[Idaho Vandals men's basketball|Idaho]].  Frank Garza is [[Spanish Americans|Spanish-American]].  Garza watched video tapes that his father collected of former NBA post players like [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]] and attempted to recreate their moves.<ref name="emmert">{{cite web|first=Mark|last=Emmert|title=Iowa's Luka Garza studies the masters in attempt to become elite scorer|url=https://www.hawkcentral.com/story/sports/college/iowa/2019/02/06/iowa-hawkeyes-basketball-indiana-hoosiers-luka-garza-old-school-mentality-years-studying-nba-greats/2783484002/|website=HawkCentral.com|date=February 6, 2019|access-date=December 13, 2019}}</ref> His mother, Šejla Muftić, who is from [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]], played professional basketball in Europe.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Luka Garza explains why he turned down Team USA, leaves Europe's door open |url=https://basketnews.com/news-192278-luka-garza-explains-why-he-turned-down-team-usa-leaves-europes-door-open.html |access-date=2024-10-19 |website=basketnews.com |language=en}}</ref>

Garza stood {{height|ft=6|in=7}} as a freshman attending [[Maret School]] in Washington, D.C., but was not able to [[slam dunk|dunk]] a basketball until he was a sophomore.<ref name=emmert/> In high school, Garza was coached by [[Chuck Driesell]], son of [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame|Basketball Hall of Fame]] coach [[Lefty Driesell]].<ref name="feinstein">{{cite web|first=John|last=Feinstein|title=Iowa's Luka Garza is a rising star, and Lefty Driesell has been saying it for years|url=https://www.thegazette.com/subject/sports/iowas-luka-garza-is-a-rising-star-and-lefty-driesell-has-been-saying-it-for-years-20190322|work=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]]|date=March 22, 2019|access-date=December 13, 2019}}</ref> As a senior, Garza averaged 24.6 points, 11.7 rebounds and 2.5 blocks per game. He led Maret to the [[District of Columbia State Athletic Association]] (DCSAA) title game and earned D.C. [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] honors.<ref name="whooley">{{cite web|first=Connor|last=Whooley|title=Iowa hoops commit Luke Garza wins Washington, D.C., Gatorade Player of the Year|url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/college/iowa-hoops-commit-luke-garza-wins-washington-gatorade-player-the-year/Ien6Fkqt2gbaiVl59OPx3K/|work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|date=March 20, 2017|access-date=December 13, 2019|archive-date=December 13, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191213183848/https://www.ajc.com/sports/college/iowa-hoops-commit-luke-garza-wins-washington-gatorade-player-the-year/Ien6Fkqt2gbaiVl59OPx3K/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Garza left as his school's all-time leading scorer, with 1,993 points.<ref name="mullan">{{cite news|first=Dillon|last=Mullan|title=Maret big man Luka Garza wins D.C. Gatorade Player of the Year|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/recruiting-insider/wp/2017/03/21/maret-big-man-luka-garza-wins-d-c-gatorade-player-of-the-year/|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|date=March 21, 2017|access-date=December 13, 2019}}</ref>

Garza was a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and chose to play college basketball for [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]] over offers from [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]], [[Georgia Bulldogs men's basketball|Georgia]] and [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]], among others.<ref name="goodwin">{{cite web|first=Cody|last=Goodwin|title=Four-star big man Luka Garza commits to Iowa hoops|url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/high-school/recruiting/2016/09/10/four-star-big-man-luke-garza-commits-iowa-hoops/90135362/|website=[[The Des Moines Register]]|date=September 10, 2016|access-date=December 13, 2019}}</ref>

==College career==
===Freshman season (2017–2018)===
In his college debut versus [[Chicago State Cougars men's basketball|Chicago State]], Garza had 16 points. He had his first double-double of 11 points and 13 rebounds the following game in a victory over [[Alabama State Hornets men's basketball|Alabama State]] and was named [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] freshman of the week.<ref name="IaMEFWMBH">{{cite web|title=Iowa and Minnesota Earn First Weekly Men's Basketball Honors: Minnesota's Jordan Murphy earns Player of the Week honors; Hawkeyes' Luka Garza named Freshmen of the Week|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111317aab.html|website=BigTen.org|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|date=November 13, 2017|access-date=November 13, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171114040206/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111317aab.html|archive-date=November 14, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> As a freshman, Garza averaged 12.1 points and 6.4 rebounds per game.<ref name="tear">{{cite news|title=Sophomore Luka Garza on a tear for surging Hawkeyes|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2019/02/05/sophomore-luka-garza-on-a-tear-for-surging-hawkeyes/39012409/|work=[[USA Today]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=February 5, 2019|access-date=December 15, 2019}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Detroit Pistons (2021–2022)===
Garza was selected with the 52nd overall pick by the [[Detroit Pistons]] in the [[2021 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2021 NBA Draft results: Picks 1-60|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2021-nba-draft-results-picks-1-60|website=NBA.com|date=July 31, 2021|access-date=July 31, 2021}}</ref> After a standout [[2021 NBA Summer League|Summer League]] performance, he was signed to a [[two-way contract]] by the Pistons and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Motor City Cruise]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Detroit Pistons Sign Luka Garza and Chris Smith to Two-Way Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-luka-garza-and-chris-smith-two-way-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=August 17, 2021|access-date=September 25, 2021}}</ref> On September 24, the team announced they had converted Garza's contract from a two-way to a standard deal.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Pistons PR|title=The Detroit Pistons announced today that the team has converted center Luka Garza's two-way contract to a standard NBA contract. Terms of the contract were not disclosed.|number=1441448414433189890|user=Pistons_PR|date=September 24, 2021|access-date=September 24, 2021}}</ref>

On October 23, Garza made his NBA debut, posting three points, two rebounds, two steals, and an assist across six minutes of play in a 97–82 loss to the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2022–2025)===
On August 23, 2022, Garza signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Taylor|last=Nardinger|title=Timberwolves Sign CJ Elleby and Luka Garza|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-cj-elleby-and-luka-garza|website=NBA.com|date=August 23, 2022|access-date=August 24, 2022}}</ref> On October 15, the Timberwolves converted his deal to a [[two-way contract]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Timberwolves sign Luka Garza to 2-way deal {{!}} Sports Illustrated Minnesota Sports, News, Analysis, and More|url=https://www.si.com/fannation/bringmethesports/.amp/timberwolves/report-timberwolves-sign-luka-garza-to-2-way-deal|website=SI.com|date=October 15, 2022|access-date=October 25, 2022}}</ref> Garza was named captain of Team Luka for the G League's inaugural Next Up Game for the 2022–23 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Wolves' Garza And Ignite's Henderson Named Captains For NBA G League Next Up Game|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-garza-and-ignites-henderson-named-captains-for-nba-g-league-next-up-game|website=NBA.com|date=February 7, 2023|access-date=March 8, 2023}}</ref> He was named the MVP of the game after leading his team to a 178–162 victory over Team [[Scoot Henderson|Scoot]], logging 23 points and eight rebounds.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Chris|last=Schad|title=Timberwolves' Luka Garza wins MVP in NBA G-League's 'Next Up' Game|url=https://www.si.com/fannation/bringmethesports/timberwolves/mn-timberwolves-luka-garza-wins-mvp-in-nba-g-leagues-next-up-game|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=February 23, 2023|access-date=March 8, 2023}}</ref>

On July 3, 2023, Garza signed another two-way contract with the Timberwolves.<ref>{{cite web|first=Taylor|last=Nardinger|title=Timberwolves Re-Sign Luka Garza|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-re-sign-luka-garza|website=NBA.com|date=July 3, 2023|access-date=July 6, 2023}}</ref>

On April 4, 2024, Garza's contract was converted to a standard NBA contract, dropping his two-way status and allowing him to play for the Timberwolves during the [[2024 NBA playoffs]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Timberwolves Convert Luka Garza to Standard NBA Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-convert-luka-garza-to-standard-nba-contract|website=NBA.com|date=April 4, 2024|access-date=April 4, 2024}}</ref> This came the day after a game against the [[Toronto Raptors]] in which Garza scored 16 points in nine minutes, his then-season high.

On July 6, 2024, Garza re-signed with the Timberwolves.<ref>{{cite web|title=Timberwolves Re-Sign Luka Garza|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-re-sign-luka-garza-24|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2024|access-date=July 7, 2024}}</ref>

===Boston Celtics (2025–present)===
On July 7, 2025, Garza signed a two-year, $5.5 million contract with the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Ryan |first=Conor |date=June 30, 2025 |title=Celtics reportedly sign big man Luka Garza to 2-year contract |url=https://www.boston.com/sports/boston-celtics/2025/06/30/boston-celtics-luka-garza-nba-basketball-free-agency-luke-kornet/ |access-date=July 1, 2025 |website=Boston.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/070725-press-release-celtics-sign-luka-garza-and-josh-minott|title=Celtics Sign Luka Garza and Josh Minott|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2025}}</ref> On March 20, 2026, Garza had a then career-high 22 points, as well as 7 rebounds (6 offensive) in a 117-112 win against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{citeweb|url=https://www.bostonherald.com/2026/03/20/key-reserve-helps-celtics-rally-past-zombie-grizzlies-avoid-upset/|title=Key reserve helps Celtics rally past zombie Grizzlies, avoid upset|last=Cox|first=Zack|publisher=[[Boston Herald]]|date=March 20, 2026|accessdate=March 20, 2026}}</ref> On April 12, Garza had a career-high 27 points, as well as 12 rebounds, in a 113-108 victory over the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{citeweb|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/04/12/sports/nba-celtics-magic-game-score-garza/?event=event12|title=With eight players resting, Celtics reserves pull off inspiring victory over play-in-bound Magic|last=Himmelsbach|first=Adam|publisher=[[The Boston Globe]]|date=April 12, 2026|accessdate=April 12, 2026}}</ref>

==National team career==
In September 2020, Garza expressed his interest to represent the [[Bosnia and Herzegovina men's national basketball team|Bosnia and Herzegovina national team]] internationally.<ref>{{cite web|first=David|last=Eickholt|title=Luka Garza aiming to play on Bosnia's national team|url=https://247sports.com/college/iowa/Article/Luka-Garza-Josef-Nurkic-Bosnia-National-Team-Iowa-Hawkeyes-Basketball-Frank-Garza--151050745/|website=247sports.com|date=September 4, 2020|access-date=July 21, 2021}}</ref> In December 2021, Garza told a reporter that he finished the process of obtaining dual citizenship.<ref>{{cite web|title=Luka Garza dobio državljanstvo BiH, može igrati za reprezentaciju|url=https://sportsport.ba/kosarka/luka-garza-drzavljanstvo-bih-nastup-reprezentacija/415040|website=SportSport.ba|date=December 22, 2021 |access-date=January 2, 2022|language=bs}}</ref> He made his debut in August 2023 in an Olympic qualifiers game against Portugal, finishing the match with 15 points and 12 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|first=Haris|last=Mrkonja|title=Zmajevi savladali Portugal teže od očekivanog, sljedeća Poljska|url=https://n1info.ba/sport-klub/kosarka/zmajevi-savladali-portugal-teze-od-ocekivanog-sljedeca-madjarska/|website=N1Info.ba|date=August 13, 2023|access-date=August 23, 2023}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Both of Garza's parents have [[basketball]] experience: his [[Spanish-American]] father, Frank Garza, played collegiately at [[Idaho Vandals men's basketball|Idaho]], and his [[Bosniak]] mother, Šejla Muftić, played professionally in Europe. Garza's paternal grandfather, James Halm, played college basketball for [[Hawaii Rainbow Warriors men's basketball|Hawaii]]. His maternal uncle through marriage, [[Teoman Alibegović]], husband of his mother's sister Lejla Muftić, was at one point the [[Slovenia men%27s national basketball team#Top scorers|all-time leading scorer]] for the [[Slovenia national basketball team]].<ref name="goldwein">{{cite news|first=Eric|last=Goldwein|title=Maret's Luka Garza keeps family basketball tradition going|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/recruiting-insider/wp/2016/02/25/marets-luka-garza-keeps-family-basketball-tradition-going/|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|date=February 25, 2016|access-date=February 25, 2016}}</ref> Garza's cousins [[Amar Alibegović]], Mirza Alibegović, and Denis Alibegović are all professional basketball players in Europe. His maternal grandfather, [[Refik Muftić]], was an accomplished [[association football]] goalkeeper, spending most of his career with [[FK Sarajevo]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Košarkaš Luka Garza: Želim predstavljati BiH|url=https://ba.voanews.com/a/kosarkas-luka-garza-zelim-predstavljati-bih/5614340.html|work=Glas Amerike|date=October 9, 2020|access-date=July 7, 2021|language=bs}}</ref>

Since 2022, Garza has been in a relationship with Victoria Vidi.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/basketball/luka-garza-girlfriend | title=Who is Luka Garza Girlfriend ? All you need to know }}</ref>
